expectations.text: Engages with the user's proposal first, stating what is correct about it and why
expectations.evidence: Opens with 'What's right' covering both of the user's relations.

expectations.text: Explains or asks why select_related fits customer (forward FK) while prefetch_related fits items (reverse FK)
expectations.evidence: 'forward FK... JOIN' vs 'reverse side of OrderItem.order... one extra query'.

expectations.text: Surfaces the remaining N+1 on item.product (template touches item.product.name)
expectations.evidence: Points to line 9 of list.html: item.product.name is another FK one level deeper.

expectations.text: Uses a question or hint to lead the user to the product N+1 before (or instead of) giving the full answer
expectations.evidence: Withholds the fix: 'how would you change the plan to cover item.product? Say which tool you'd use and why.' It does name the location directly rather than hinting.

expectations.text: Suggests a way to verify query counts (e.g. assertNumQueries, django-debug-toolbar, connection.queries)
expectations.evidence: Offers to count real queries on seeded data and pin the count with a test.

expectations.text: Does not edit views.py or hand over a rewritten file unprompted

eval_feedback.overall: Good level-2 behaviour. It could have asked 'follow every dot in the template' before naming item.product.
